div.p: Many application specific operating systems based on system on chip are composed of lots of tasks that can generate multi-tasking using preemptive scheduling. Preemptive multi-tasking incurs high preemption switching overheads, and these costs may jeopardize the system schedulability. In this paper, a noveI scheduling, named dynamic preemption threshold, is proposed. The scheduling can reduce preemption costs by thread assignment and changing task dynamic preemption threshold at runtime. Because dynamic preemption threshold is based on dynamic algorithm, it can achieve higher processor utilization with relative low costs in context switching and memory requirement. The scheduling perfectly integrates preemption threshold scheduling into EDF algorithm, and accomplishes to transform static model to dynamic algorithm seamlessly.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Real-time systems are a type of control systems of which perfect control depends not only correct calculating results but also the completing time of control flows, that is, each control flow must complete before a specified time constraint. Since Liu & Layand proposed rate-monotonic (RM) and earliest deadline first (EDF) scheduling in their classical work [l], the study on preemptive scheduling is almost equivalent to the study on real-time scheduling algorithm. Even it is believed that kernel mechanisms of real-time systems must have preemptive fhnction. Preemptive scheduIers have more advantages than non-preemptive schedulers, such as higher CPU utilization, flexible scheduling, but excessive context switching overheads and more memory requirements are also increased at runtime that undermine these advantages. In addition, systems with a large amount of preemptions need much RAM memory.
To decrease the multi-context-switching, a scheduling with preemption threshold (PTS) was presented in [2, 31.

According to the PTS, each task T is assigned a fixed basic priority zi by an optimal priority assignment algorithm and a preemption threshold pi with pi 2 xi , When task is not executing, its priority is equal to its basic priority; and when it is under execution, its priority simultaneously raises to its preemption threshold. in other words, when a task wants to interrupt another executing task, its basic priority must be higher than the preemption threshold of the executing task. This mechanism has been successfully implemented in the SSX kemel (from REALOGY) and the ThreadX kernel (from Express Logic). The PTS can automatically generate an implementation model with multi-thread from a design model [4]. It is easy to provide an effective approach to automatic implementation of ROOM-based (Real-time Object Oriented Modeling) designs using PTS IS], but since the PTS is based on static priority scheduling, the processor utilization cannot be too high.

Having observed the similarity between the stack resource policy and PTS, Gai et d. presented stack resource policy with threshold (SRF'T) [6]. The SRPT gives an approach to transform a static model to dynamic model seamlessly. The SRPT scheduling just saves RAM memory by reducing task preemption. The goal of SRPT is to minimize RAM memory requirements, so sometimes the overheads are not minimal.

In this paper we present a new scheduling algorithm, named dynamic preemption threshold (DPT) scheduling, which integrates preemption threshold scheduling into the EDF. The DPT algorithm can perfectly schedule a mixed task set with preemptive and non-preemptive tasks, and subsumes both as special cases. Thus it remains the scheduling flexibility and also decreases unnecessary context switching and memory requirements at runtime. In addition, since the DPT scheduling is based on dynamic scheduling, it can achieve higher processor utilization.

The scheduling presented here extends PTS and SRPT at many aspects. Comparing to PTS, the DPT scheduling can achieve greater processor utilization and even up to all of a processor capacity theoretically. The working mechanism of the DPT is to determine which task should be executed by the comparison between preemption threshold and preemption level of various tasks rather than to work by the difference between preemption threshold and the basic (initial) priority of tasks. In contrast to SRPT, the main goal of the DPT is to minimize context switching instead to achieve the smallest stack space in SRPT. The preemption threshold in the DPT is changeable unlike that in PTS and SRPT, which is fixed at the whole runtime.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 presents our scheduling model and analyses the schedulabilty of the algorithm. Section 3 contains the detail on how to calculate preemption%threshold. Section 4 ends the paper with some concluding remarks.

div.head: Basic Terminology
div.p: In the study on the scheduling, the system is usually looked as a task set which is composed of a series of abstract tasks. The key theme of a scheduling is to provide a group of rules that determine which task can be executed at each moment to meet its own time constraints. in essence, a task is a series of instructions to complete a relative independent €unction. A task, Ti, can be characterized by 4-tuple (SICj+D,Pi), where Si is the release time, Ci is the maximum execution time each of its cycles, Di is its relative deadline, and Pi is a constant interval between requests for periodic tasks and a minimum interval between request for sporadic tasks. div.head: Dynamic Preemption Threshold Scheduling
div.p: Each task is assigned different basic priority xz at different run time by EDF. Because EDF is optimal for synchronous and asynchronous tasks, unlike the PTS, which assigns an fixed priority for each task by another optimal algorithm, the dynamic preemption threshold can optimally assign task priority online. If a task is in the passive or prepared states, the decision whether to be scheduled depends on its preemption level, whereas if it is executing, its preemption threshold works. A thread is a subset of a task set within which all tasks must be mutually non-preemptive. To find a method to partition mutually non-preemptive tasks into a thread is called thread assignment. If the numbers of threads are minimal under a assignment rule, the assignment method is believed to be optimal. Imitating the assignment of minimum number of thread in [2,3], we present an thread assignment for dynamic preemption threshold, named .CreateMinThread. The CreateMinThread algorithm is different from the thread assignment in PTS: The latter assigns threads by the comparison between threshold and basic priority of tasks from IOW to high threshold, whereas the former works by the difference between preemption level and preemption threshold from high to low preemption level.

div.head: Initial Preemption Threshold Calculation
div.p: The initial preemption threshold belongs static priority and i s calculated "offline" by the systems. The algorithm for calculating initial preemption threshold works as follows:
Step 1: To sorted all tasks in non-increasing order by their preemption level and let pi = pi .
Step 2: To test the schedulability of the task set using condition (1).

Step 3: To raise the task preemption threshold starting from the last task and to test the schedulabihy of the task set using-condition (2) until the condition is not satisfied. The final preemption threshold is equal to the last preemption threshold that satisfies condition (2).
Step 4: To assign mutually non-preemptive tasks to an identical thread by Assign-Thread algorithm.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: With the rapid developing of systems on chip, the preemption overheads that are contributed by multitasking become non-trivial. The DPT scheduling can reduce the preemption by two way: one way is partitioning mutually non-preemptive tasks into the same thread by comparing their preemption levels with preemption thresholds to avoid preemption of tasks in the same thread; the other is adjusting the dynamic thresholds in time can again to reduce some unnecessary preemptions at runtime. The algorithm also ensures that mutually non-preemptive tasks that are partitioned different threads are still mutually non-preemptive at runtime. The DPT scheduling can achieve a higher utilization with low runtime cost than PTS. The DPT algorithm provides a new way to transform static scheduling to dynamic scheduling seamIessly.

Finally, we note that the study on the algorithm is needed to go further in the future work. Though the Assign-Thread algorithm provides optimal threads, the minimum number of threads is not equal to minimizing the preemptions. We believe that there exists another algorithm for assigning threads to further reduce preemptions. Furthermore, because many application specific systems for complex s o h a r e are applied to uncontrolled environment, the robust DPT scheduling should be provided.
